title: Bedrock says it's advancing construction with AI-driven excavators
excerpt: Bedrock Robotics said its excavators equipped with its autonomous AI system are working without human operators on three sites in Texas and Nevada.
content_html:
First came self-driving cars. Now, Waymo veterans are building autonomous construction equipment.

By Rya Jetha

You're currently following this author! Want to unfollow? Unsubscribe via the link in your email.

Self-driving cars have spent years learning the rules of the road. Now, several Waymo veterans are trying to apply those lessons to a far less predictable environment: construction sites.

San Francisco-based Bedrock Robotics said Monday that excavators equipped with its autonomous AI system are now working without human operators on three commercial sites in Texas and Nevada. Machines equipped with Bedrock's technology are digging and moving earth on multiple projects, including a water treatment facility.

The appeal of automating construction is clear. The industry faces labor shortages, high rates of worker deaths, and chronic delays. More than 40% of the construction workforce is projected to retire by 2031, according to the National Center for Construction Education and Research.

A construction site, however, is less predictable than a factory floor. Terrain, crews, and tasks can change by the day on construction sites, and it remains unclear whether autonomous machines can reliably adapt to changing conditions reliably and cheaply enough for contractors to embrace them.

Bedrock's technology remains in early stages. For now, its autonomous AI system works only on excavators, which are deployed on three sites.

"It would be fair to say it's a limited test," Vineet Kamat, a University of Michigan construction management professor, told Business Insider.

Bedrock, valued at $1.75 billion, was founded in 2024 to automate construction and accelerate housing, data center, and other infrastructure projects.

Bedrock's founders learned from Waymo's early days

Bedrock's cofounder and chief technology officer, Kevin Peterson, compared the company's progress to Waymo's early days, when its autonomous cars operated within just a few city blocks.

"If you look at the scaling Waymo did year by year, we think our scaling will occur in the same way," he told Business Insider.

Bedrock retrofits excavators with sensors and onboard computing, enabling them to perceive their surroundings, plan their movements, and carry out tasks set by a site manager. The next technical test is whether the same system can transfer to other equipment, including bulldozers, dump trucks, and loaders.

"There are open questions about that transfer," Peterson said. "We think it will work, but it will be hard."

In the near term, Peterson expects humans to remain on construction sites. He said that humanoid robots could eventually take on more work if the technology matures and fewer people enter the industry.

"The physical economy is the next great frontier for machine learning," cofounder and CEO Boris Sofman, who spent nearly five years bringing Waymo's autonomous cars to freeways and leading its trucking division, said in a press release.

Autonomous systems in construction are designed for narrow, repetitive jobs. Bedrock is betting that lessons from Waymo can help it build more adaptable AI that eventually works across multiple types of construction equipment and coordinates entire fleets.

Bedrock faces some hurdles in the construction industry

A major hurdle for Bedrock and its competitors will be convincing contractors that the technology is worth the money, University of Michigan's Kamat said. Construction companies often operate on thin margins and win work through competitive bidding, leaving little room for costly experiments.

"For a contractor to take a leap and invest a few hundred thousand dollars in robotics equipment, they need to be sure it will generate a return on investment," he said.

Once autonomous construction companies prove themselves, "everybody will want in," Kamat added.

Bedrock's competitors include both startups and heavy-equipment giants. Companies like Built Robotics deploy autonomous machines on solar and data-center projects, including at Meta's Hyperion data center in Louisiana.

Another giant, Caterpillar, has more than 800 autonomous haul trucks, while AIM Intelligent Machines retrofits machinery to operate autonomously at construction, mining, and defense sites.

Fernanda Leite, a civil engineering professor and vice president for research at the University of Texas at Austin, expects construction sites to look more like airports in the near term — where highly automated systems operate alongside skilled workers.

"The robot is competing against a highly flexible, general-purpose system," she said, "which is a highly trained human."

She has a bachelor’s degree in history and politics from Pomona College and a master’s in history from the University of Cambridge. Rya lives in San Francisco. content_html_zh:
首先是自动驾驶汽车。 现在，Waymo 的资深人士正在建造自主施工设备。

作者：Rya Jetha 您目前正在关注该作者！ 想要取消关注吗？ 通过电子邮件中的链接取消订阅。

自动驾驶汽车花了数年时间来学习道路规则。 现在，几位 Waymo 资深人士正试图将这些经验教训应用到一个难以预测的环境：建筑工地。

总部位于旧金山的 Bedrock Robotics 周一表示，配备自主人工智能系统的挖掘机目前在德克萨斯州和内华达州的三个商业场所无需人工操作即可工作。 配备 Bedrock 技术的机器正在多个项目中挖掘和运土，其中包括水处理设施。

自动化施工的吸引力是显而易见的。 该行业面临劳动力短缺、工人死亡率高和长期延误的问题。 据国家建筑教育与研究中心称，预计到 2031 年，超过 40% 的建筑工人将退休。

然而，建筑工地比工厂车间更难以预测。 建筑工地上的地形、人员和任务每天都会发生变化，目前还不清楚自主机器是否能够可靠地适应不断变化的条件，并且成本足够低，足以让承包商接受它们。

Bedrock 的技术仍处于早期阶段。 目前，其自主人工智能系统仅适用于部署在三个站点的挖掘机。

密歇根大学建筑管理教授维尼特·卡马特 (Vineet Kamat) 告诉《商业内幕》：“可以公平地说，这是一次有限的测试。”

Bedrock 估值 17.5 亿美元，成立于 2024 年，旨在实现建筑自动化并加速住房、数据中心和其他基础设施项目。

Bedrock 的创始人向 Waymo 早期学习

Bedrock 的联合创始人兼首席技术官 Kevin Peterson 将公司的进展与 Waymo 的早期发展进行了比较，当时其自动驾驶汽车仅在几个城市街区内运行。

“如果你看看 Waymo 逐年扩张的规模，我们认为我们的扩张也会以同样的方式发生，”他告诉《商业内幕》。

Bedrock 对挖掘机进行了改造，配备了传感器和机载计算装置，使挖掘机能够感知周围环境、规划其运动并执行现场经理设定的任务。 接下来的技术测试是同一系统是否可以转移到其他设备上，包括推土机、自卸车、装载机等。

“关于这次转会还存在一些悬而未决的问题，”彼得森说。 “我们认为这会起作用，但会很困难。”

彼得森预计，短期内人类仍将留在建筑工地上。 他表示，如果技术成熟并且进入该行业的人数减少，人形机器人最终可能会承担更多的工作。

“实体经济是机器学习的下一个伟大前沿，”联合创始人兼首席执行官鲍里斯·索夫曼 (Boris Sofman) 在一份新闻稿中表示，他花了近五年的时间将 Waymo 的自动驾驶汽车带到高速公路上并领导其卡车运输部门。

建筑中的自主系统是为狭窄的、重复性的工作而设计的。 Bedrock 押注 Waymo 的经验教训可以帮助其构建适应性更强的人工智能，最终适用于多种类型的建筑设备并协调整个车队。

基岩在建筑行业面临一些障碍

密歇根大学的卡马特表示，Bedrock 及其竞争对手面临的一个主要障碍是让承包商相信该技术物有所值。 建筑公司通常利润微薄，通过竞标赢得工作，几乎没有空间进行昂贵的实验。

他说：“对于要迈出一步并在机器人设备上投资数十万美元的承包商来说，他们需要确保它将产生投资回报。”

卡马特补充说，一旦自主建筑公司证明自己，“每个人都会想加入”。

Bedrock 的竞争对手包括初创公司和重型设备巨头。 Built Robotics 等公司在太阳能和数据中心项目上部署自主机器，其中包括路易斯安那州 Meta 的 Hyperion 数据中心。

另一家巨头卡特彼勒拥有 800 多辆自动运输卡车，而 AIM 智能机器公司则对机械进行改造，使其能够在建筑、采矿和国防场所自动运行。

德克萨斯大学奥斯汀分校土木工程教授兼研究副校长费尔南达·莱特 (Fernanda Leite) 预计，短期内建筑工地将更像机场，高度自动化的系统与熟练工人一起运行。

“机器人正在与一个高度灵活的通用系统竞争，”她说，“这是一个训练有素的人类。”
